tasks.name: `atm migrate`: automatic move to .agentic-task-manager/
tasks.description: Both runtimes. `atm migrate [--json]`: if .agentic-task-manager/tasks.json exists and a legacy file too, move nothing and print a warning (exit 0). If only a legacy tasks.json exists (docs/ or root): create the folder, `git mv` it when tracked (plain move otherwise); for the legacy tasks-dashboard.html next to it: `git rm --cached` if tracked, then delete. Always ensure .agentic-task-manager/.gitignore contains tasks-dashboard.html, .server.json, claims.json, .lock/ (idempotent; preserve user lines). Copy the plugin's templates/tasks-dashboard.html into the folder if missing or older (compare atm-dashboard-version meta numerically; shared helper `ensure_dashboard`). Prints one line describing what moved (or nothing to do). Never commits. Conformance scenarios: tracked/untracked, docs/ and root legacy, both locations present, already migrated (idempotent), non-git directory, gitignore merging.

tasks.name: `atm serve` in Python: start/stop/status
tasks.description: atm.py `serve [start|stop|status] [--open] [--port N]`. start: run `migrate` checks' ensure_dashboard, then spawn a detached child (new session, stdio to .agentic-task-manager/.server.log) running a stdlib http.server bound to 127.0.0.1 that serves the folder by absolute path (works after the launching shell's cwd is deleted) and answers GET /__atm/whoami with {project folder, pid, runtime}. Port: --port or 8000, else the next free port up to 8099. Record {pid, port, folder, runtime, started_at} in .agentic-task-manager/.server.json. If a record exists and whoami at that port answers with this folder: report its URL instead of starting. Stale record (pid gone or whoami mismatch): remove it and start. stop: only kill the pid if whoami confirms it is this folder's server, then remove the record; otherwise just clean the record and say so. status: running (URL, pid, uptime) or not running. Output: the URL http://localhost:PORT/tasks-dashboard.html; --open opens it (open / xdg-open). Server survives the parent process exiting.

tasks.name: `atm serve` in Node, plus serve tests for both
tasks.description: atm.mjs equivalent of T-065 (node:http static server with correct content types for .html/.json, detached child via spawn({detached:true, stdio:[ignore, log, log]}).unref(), same whoami endpoint, record format and output). Conformance tests (both runtimes, temp project, a test port range to avoid 8000): start then status reports it and the dashboard and tasks.json are served; second start reuses; port in use moves to the next port; stale record (fake pid) is cleaned; stop refuses to kill a pid whose whoami doesn't match (spawn an unrelated sleeping process and record its pid); serving keeps working after the launching cwd is removed; stop leaves no process. Always stop servers in test teardown.

tasks.name: Lock directory and atomic writes
tasks.description: atm.py, per design §4 'The lock': acquire = mkdir <dir>/.lock, write owner.json {host, pid, acquired_at}; retry every 50 ms up to 10 s; break the lock only if owner is on this host and the pid is gone, or it is older than 60 s; release removes it (also on exceptions/signals). Atomic write = write temp file in the same dir, fsync, rename over target, fsync dir where supported. Expose a `with_lock(path, fn)` context helper and reuse `write_json_atomic`. Tests (tests/scripts/lock.test.mjs, driving small atm commands or a hidden `_lock-test` command): mutual exclusion between processes, stale lock from a dead pid is broken, live foreign lock times out with a clear error.

tasks.name: `atm start|done|fail|release` status commands
tasks.description: atm.py. Under the tasks lock: re-read tasks.json, validate the task exists and the transition is legal (start: todo -> in_progress, sets started_at and updated_at; done: in_progress -> done, sets completed_at; fail: in_progress -> todo with a `last_failure` note; release: in_progress -> todo). Write atomically preserving key order and 2-space formatting (unchanged tasks byte-identical). Clear exit codes and messages. Scenarios for each transition, illegal transitions, unknown id, missing file.

tasks.name: Claims with leases: store, heartbeat, claims, expiry
tasks.description: atm.py: Claims file = $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/atm/claims.json (fallback .agentic-task-manager/claims-store.json outside git), guarded by its own lock dir. Claim = {task, agent (CLAUDE_SESSION_ID or ATM_AGENT env, else host:pid), branch, worktree, claimed_at, lease_expires_at}; lease default 30 min (meta.lease_minutes overrides). start takes a claim and fails if another live claim holds the task; done/fail/release drop it; `heartbeat <id>` extends it (only for the holder); `claims [--json]` lists live claims with time left. Any command first expires stale leases: task back to todo with `last_failure: 'lease expired (agent X)'`. After every change write the gitignored snapshot .agentic-task-manager/claims.json for the dashboard. Tests incl. two worktrees of one repo seeing each other's claims and lease expiry with an injectable clock (ATM_NOW).

tasks.name: `atm next --claim` with the loop's selection rule
tasks.description: atm.py: `atm next [--phase N] [--type T] [--claim] [--json]`: lowest phase then lowest id among todo tasks whose dependencies are all done and that have no live claim; with --claim, start+claim it in the same lock section. Prints the task (JSON with --json) or exits 3 with 'no task available' (distinguishing 'blocked' from 'all done'). Conformance scenarios mirroring the dashboard's Next-up rule (dashboard/src/lib/kanban.ts) so both agree.

tasks.name: Concurrency stress test
tasks.description: tests/scripts/stress.test.mjs: a 40-task project; spawn 16 concurrent workers that loop `atm next --claim` then `atm done` until none left; assert every task done exactly once and no claim double-granted (each worker logs what it got). In parallel a reader polls tasks.json and claims.json every few ms and asserts it always parses. Run in a temp git repo with two worktrees (workers split across them). Keep the test under ~30 s.

tasks.name: tasks.json merge driver and `atm init`
tasks.description: atm.py: `atm merge-driver %O %A %B` merges task by task (design option E): union of tasks by id; same id changed on one side takes that side; changed on both: status takes the furthest along (todo < in_progress < done, blocked/skipped explicit wins over todo), timestamps take the newest, definition fields (name, description, deps, files, phase, type, requirements) changed differently on both sides = conflict (exit 1, leave conflict markers-free file plus a report on stderr); new tasks on both sides with colliding ids: keep both, renumber theirs to the next free id and rewrite dependencies that point to it within their new tasks. Writes the result to %A in the standard format. `atm init`: adds `tasks.json merge=atm` to .agentic-task-manager/.gitattributes and sets git config merge.atm.name/driver (pointing at the launcher by absolute path), idempotent.

tasks.name: Merge driver tests from the design's experiments
tasks.description: tests/scripts/merge.test.mjs: in temp repos with `atm init`, reproduce the design doc's experiments with real `git merge`: adjacent status changes (clean), finishing adjacent tasks (clean), same task claimed on both branches (clean merge, status in_progress, newest timestamp), both sides append a task (both kept, renumbered, deps rewritten), same task's description edited differently (merge fails and reports it). Plus unit scenarios for the driver directly.

tasks.name: Skills use atm for every status change; commit hygiene
tasks.description: do-task and loop-tasks: get work only via `atm next --claim` (or `atm start <id>`), finish with `atm done`, `atm fail` on failure, `atm heartbeat` roughly every 10 minutes on long tasks; never edit status/started_at/completed_at by hand (state the 6 agent rules from design §4). Commit `.agentic-task-manager/tasks.json` plus exactly the files the agent changed for this task (tracked by the agent; `git add <paths>`), never `git add -A`/`git add .`. create-tasks runs `atm init`. Remove the now-obsolete manual timestamp instructions.

tasks.name: Dashboard shows live claims
tasks.description: Load ./claims.json alongside tasks.json on every (auto-)refresh; a missing file or 404 means no claims (no error shown). src/lib/claims.ts: parse, keep live ones, map by task id. In-progress task cards and Kanban cards show the agent (short form), branch and 'claimed 12 m ago'; the detail panel shows the full claim and lease expiry. Extend the e2e tasksServer fixture to route claims.json (default 404, can serve an object). Unit tests for claims.ts (90% coverage), component/e2e tests, update screenshots if card layout changes.

tasks.name: Remote claims via refs/atm/claims (P2)
tasks.description: atm.py: opt-in with meta.coordination = 'remote'. Claiming also runs `git push origin <HEAD sha>:refs/atm/claims/<id>` and only proceeds if accepted (rejected = someone else holds it; roll back the local claim); done/fail/release/expiry push a deletion (best-effort, logged on failure). `atm claims --remote` lists remote claim refs (git ls-remote). Tests with a local bare repo as origin and two clones. Skip if it can't be done cheaply; record the reason.

tasks.name: README: Running agents in parallel
